Description: Saruke is a young Alan noblewoman and Saros's wife. Marriage connects her to the son of Boz-Uruz, while her own standing remains tied to Beler's household. These overlapping obligations give her reasons to listen carefully when relatives discuss allegiance, hospitality or military support. She wants her marriage to bring dependable cooperation rather than become a pretext for one household to demand unlimited service from the other. Direct in conversation, she asks what has actually been promised and who will bear the cost. Courtesy matters to her, but an impressive title does not settle a disagreement over provisions, shelter or the safety of those expected to travel. She can support Saros without accepting that his father's interests always coincide with hers. Nor does she assume that her own relatives will welcome every decision she makes as a wife. Young enough to be underestimated, she resents being spoken for and prefers a modest commitment she understands to a grand promise made in her name. Her generosity is practical: she would rather share what can be spared than display wealth while leaving dependants exposed. Pressure to choose between households can make her guarded, especially when an envoy treats loyalty as something already purchased by marriage. She seeks room for her own judgement within family obligations, with neither the authority of a seasoned matriarch nor a commander's appetite for battlefield distinction.
